evidence.finding: Timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC; the generic moment-in-time description does not define the hourly interval labelling or availability of each selected weather quantity.
Weather comes from CERRA, ERA5-Land and ERA5; coordinates and station identities are anonymised. Per-variable product mapping, interval/averaging semantics and publication latency are not specified.

Dataset harmonisation/resampling and gaps, possible unit mislabelling and different accumulation/measurement strategies are documented. There is no authoritative L03-specific divide-by-1000 instruction.
L03/L14 source timestamps are treated as interval ends by project convention; values are used directly. L07 uses already processed counter differences and their existing interval bounds.
L07 counter differences are assigned to the preceding/current counter timestamps; invalid intervals/gaps remain exclusions.
Original weather uses exact interval_start_utc equality; no availability metadata or publication-latency check is implemented.
Targets are exported sequentially in their input row order and verified row by row; no target shift is performed.
Selected L03 EM02 is electricity use; EM01 is the separate virtual aggregate described in the building-info note. These must not be conflated.

timing_limitation: Intended prediction at t is consumption over [t,t+1h). Current electricity interval conventions are retained, without shifting targets. The dataset documents historical reanalysis weather but not its per-variable interval semantics or availability at t. Current alignment is an assumed conditional comparison, not established operational information at t. Exact t-1h weather reduces contemporaneous dependence but does not establish publication latency.
review_method: Local PDF read with macOS PDFKit; preparation code, metadata and saved outputs inspected before implementation
